title: Lists: a shot list in code
hook: Keep a whole crew or shot list in one variable and grab any item.

warmup.q: Yesterday you used `random.randint(1, 10)`. Which numbers can it give?
options: Any whole number from 1 to 10, both ends included
warmup.explain: randint picks a whole number, and both the low and the high number can come up.

warmup.q: How many times does the body of `for i in range(3):` run?
warmup.explain: range(3) gives 0, 1, 2. That is three turns of the loop.
!= means not equal. Five is equal to five, so the question 'are they different?' is False.

why.heading: One name, many things
why.text: So far a variable held one thing. But a shot list holds many shots, and a crew list holds many people. A **list** is one variable that holds many things, in order. You keep the order, you can add to it, and you can ask for any item.

why.heading: Square brackets, commas
why.text:
Put the items in square brackets with commas between them:

`shots = ["wide", "close", "drone"]`

Text items need quotes. Numbers do not: `rates = [850, 1200, 950]`.

why.heading: Count from zero
why.text:
To grab one item, give its position in square brackets. Python counts from **0**, not 1. So `shots[0]` is `wide`, `shots[1]` is `close`. The first item is number zero. It feels odd, and then it becomes normal.

A minus number counts from the end: `shots[-1]` is the last item.

why.heading: Four handy tools
why.text:
`len(shots)` tells you how many items.

`shots.append("insert")` adds one to the end.

`"drone" in shots` answers True or False.

`shots[1] = "medium"` swaps item 1 for something new.

why.heading: The IndexError
why.text: Ask for a spot that is not there, like `shots[9]` in a list of 3, and Python says **IndexError: list index out of range**. It means: there is no item at that number. Check your count, remembering it starts at 0 and the last spot is one less than `len`.

watch.intro: Tap Run. One list, grabbed and changed in a few ways.
watch.code:
shots = ["wide", "close", "drone"]
print(shots[0])
print(shots[-1])
shots.append("insert")
print(len(shots))
print("drone" in shots)
shots[1] = "medium"
print(shots)
explain: `shots[0]` is the first item and `shots[-1]` is the last.
`append` put `insert` on the end, so `len` now says 4.
`"drone" in shots` is True because drone is in the list.
Printing a whole list shows the square brackets and single quotes. That is normal, Python is just showing it as a list.
watch.break_it: Break it on purpose: add the line `print(shots[9])` at the bottom and tap Run. The error ends with `IndexError: list index out of range`. The list only has 4 items, so spot 9 does not exist. Delete the line again.

tasks.title: First and last
tasks.task:
The crew list is ready. Print the first name, then the last name, each on its own line:

`Sam`
`Ayanda`
tasks.starter:
crew = ["Sam", "Thandi", "Lebo", "Ayanda"]
# Print the first and the last crew member
hints: The first item is at spot 0, because Python counts from zero.
For the last item you can use spot -1.

tasks.title: Grow the shot list
tasks.task:
Start with two shots. Add `drone`, then `insert` to the end. Change the first shot to `establishing`. Then print the list, then print how many shots it holds:

`['establishing', 'close', 'drone', 'insert']`
`4`
tasks.starter:
shots = ["wide", "close"]
# add two shots, change the first, then print
tasks.solution:
shots = ["wide", "close"]
shots.append("drone")
shots.append("insert")
shots[0] = "establishing"
print(shots)
print(len(shots))
hints: Use shots.append("drone") to add to the end. Do it twice, once per shot.
To change the first item: shots[0] = "establishing"
Finish with print(shots) and then print(len(shots)).

tasks.title: Is it packed?
tasks.task:
The gear list is ready. Ask `Item? `. Print `Packed` if the item is in the list, otherwise print `Missing`. Example with `gimbal`:

`Item? gimbal`
`Packed`
tasks.starter:
gear = ["camera", "tripod", "gimbal", "mic", "slate"]
item = input("Item? ")
# print Packed or Missing
hints: You need an if and an else. The question is: is item in gear?
The test line is: if item in gear:
if item in gear: then print("Packed"), else: then print("Missing"). Indent each print by 4 spaces.

recap: A list holds many things in order: `["a", "b", "c"]`.
Spots count from 0. `-1` is the last item.
`mylist[1] = x` changes an item. A spot that does not exist gives IndexError.

words.meaning: One variable that holds many items in order.
An item's position in the list. The first is 0.
Add an item to the end of a list.
You asked for a spot the list does not have.
